_description: Fixture 3 — Insufficient evidence. Tests unsupported claim rate metric. Two claims have no matching evidence.
research_question: What is the economic impact of remote work adoption since 2020?

report.executive_summary: The shift to remote work since 2020 has significantly altered urban commercial real estate markets and worker productivity patterns. [SOURCE 1] Productivity outcomes remain contested across industries. [SOURCE 2]
key_findings: Office vacancy rates in major US cities reached 19.6% in Q3 2023, the highest since 1990. [SOURCE 1]
Remote workers report 13% higher productivity on average according to Stanford research. [SOURCE 2]
Remote work has permanently eliminated all gender pay gap differences in knowledge work.
Fully remote companies have 40% lower employee turnover than in-office companies.
report.limitations: Remote work data post-2020 covers an atypical period of pandemic disruption.

evidence.content: US office vacancy rates reached 19.6% nationally in Q3 2023, the highest level since 1990, driven by hybrid and remote work adoption reducing demand for commercial space (CBRE Research, 2023).

A Stanford University study of 16,000 workers over 9 months found that remote workers were 13% more productive than their in-office counterparts, attributed to fewer breaks, sick days, and a quieter work environment.
